title: ‘Hanuman Ansh’ Indian Sleeper Hit’s International Distribution Strategy Unveiled by ‘K.G.F,’ ‘Kantara’ Outfit Hombale Films (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Indian devotional film “Hanuman Ansh” has grossed more than $3.5 million outside its home territory since Hombale Films took it to international aud
body:
Indian devotional film “Hanuman Ansh” has grossed more than $3.5 million outside its home territory since Hombale Films took it to international audiences, and the company behind the blockbuster “K.G.F” and “Kantara” franchises has now detailed how it engineered the run.

	Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi and adapted from his book “Divine Detour: That Changed My Life,” the film follows Lakshman Das, a boy who leaves home after his mother dies, searching for the divine. Years of wandering and meditation later, he becomes the saint Neem Karoli Baba, known to devotees as Maharaj-ji. Shobhinaw Satyaa plays the title role opposite Chandan Anand, with Vihaan Shedge as the teenage Maharaj-ji and Anil Rastogi and Purnima Tiwari in supporting roles. Chaturvedi produced with Ragini Sona, Namrata G. Singh and Anupriya A. Nagar under his Swambhu Media Network banner.
	

	“Our strategy involved taking ownership of all global territories and collaborating with the biggest local partners in each region to ensure the best possible release footprint. By leveraging the data and learnings from our previous releases like ‘Mahavatar Narsimha,’ we were able to tap into the right locations and cinema chains. This targeted approach has yielded spectacular numbers,” says Hombale Films producer Chaluve Gowda.


	The Bengaluru banner partnered with Phars in the GCC and Prathyangara in North America, and the film opened internationally on Sept. 11. It marks a first for the company.

	“‘Hanuman Ansh’ is the first film outside of our own productions that we have full fledgedly distributed internationally. We truly believed in this project, as it perfectly aligns with our vision of taking Indian stories global,” Gowda says.
	

	North America leads the overseas tally, with $1.8 million from the U.S. and Canada, according to Hombale’s territory figures. Australia and New Zealand contributed $606,716 and the Gulf Cooperation Council region $577,870, with the U.K. adding $269,837. Singapore brought in $61,334 and Europe $41,171, while the rest of the world accounted for $483,006.

	Hombale previously backed the animated “Mahavatar Narsimha,” which went on to do more than INR300 crore ($31.3 million) in business.

	At home, the film has been a sleeper. Made for approximately INR2 crore ($209,000), “Hanuman Ansh” opened in India on Aug. 7 on some 250 screens through Cinépolis India. Word of mouth pushed it past 2,000 screens, and it has since grossed INR340.7 crore ($35.5 million) in seven weeks. 

	Chaturvedi has planned the film as the first part of a trilogy. 

	“We will always support the makers in bringing their ultimate vision to life. These are exactly the kinds of stories we want to champion as a production house, and we will continue to back creators who dare to tell such grand stories with all their heart,” Gowda says.

schema.headline: ‘Hanuman Ansh’ Indian Sleeper Hit’s International Distribution Strategy Unveiled by ‘K.G.F,’ ‘Kantara’ Outfit Hombale Films (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Scarlett Johansson Takes Break From Filming Overseas for ‘Paper Tiger’ NYFF Premiere After Skipping Cannes: ‘I’m Hallucinating’
description: A very jet-lagged Scarlett Johansson reunited with co-stars Adam Driver and Miles Teller for the New York Film Festival premiere of “Paper Tiger,” w
body:
A very jet-lagged Scarlett Johansson reunited with co-stars Adam Driver and Miles Teller for the New York Film Festival premiere of “Paper Tiger,” which kicked off the festival’s 64th edition.

	“I’m hallucinating,” said Johansson, who just got off a long international flight, where she’s filming another movie. “It’s 5 in the morning — which is a great time to be doing an interview on stage.”


	“Paper Tiger” premiered in May at the Cannes Film Festival. However, this marked Johansson’s first time watching the movie (at least in a festival setting); she missed the Cannes premiere because she was shooting yet another movie, “The Exorcist: Martyrs.” 
	

	“Don’t rub it in!” Johansson joked about her absence on the French Riviera.

	Set in 1986, “Paper Tiger” follows two brothers, Irwin and Gary Pearl, whose get-rich-quick scheme to help clean up the Gowanus Canal lands them in the crosshairs of the Russian mafia. Johansson plays Linda, wife of Teller’s character.

	Johansson, Driver and Teller walked the red carpet with Gray at Lincoln Center’s Alice Tully Hall and sat for a post-screening Q&A, during which they spoke about their close camaraderie during production.

	“No work required. There’s a mutual admiration between the four of us,” Driver said. “A set culture comes from the top down, and James sets a culture where everyone feels free. We immediately felt comfortable with each other.”

	Added Gray, “We had a nauseatingly lovely set. I love them. I’m not on the Today show. I’m telling you the truth.”
	



	

					Scarlett Johansson, Miles Teller and Adam Driver introduce “Paper Tiger” during the 64th New York Film Festival.
									Getty Images for FLC
	



	Before the screening began, Gray took the stage and consciously kept his intro remarks short and sweet.

	“When I was in film school many years ago, students would show their films, and the students that talked the most [before] often made the very worst movies,” he said. “So I am going to speak very briefly.”

	Gray praised the producers and actors who helped bring the film to life and reflected on his early dreams of being a filmmaker.

	“I can’t help but remember my mother and father when I said I wanted to be a movie director. ‘How are you ever going to do that?’ And here I am,” Gray said. “I’m not sure the lesson in that.”

	NYFF artistic director Dennis Lim introduced Gray as “one of the great living American filmmakers” and praised the director for championing a “singular” artistic vision.

	“It’s not easy to make personal films in the current landscape of American cinema,” Lim said. “The fact that there are 24 executive producers credited on this film, like, who speaks to that.”

	New York Film Festival’s 64th edition, which runs through Oct. 12, will host the world premieres of “Artificial,” Luca Guadagnino’s buzzy movie about OpenAI founder Sam Altman; Ava DuVernay’s documentary “14th”; director Tony Gilroy’s music drama “Behemoth!” with Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde and Will Arnett; and Takashi Yamazaki’s kaiju sequel “Godzilla Minus Zero.”

	“Premiere status is never the be-all and end-all for us,” NYFF artistic director Dennis Lim told Variety ahead of opening night. “Timing is always part of it. But I think we’ve proved in the last few years that we create a pretty interesting context for the launch of a film.”



	

					“Paper Tiger” filmmaker James Gray (center) with the film’s stars Roman Engel, Miles Teller, Scarlett Johansson, Adam Driver and Gavin Goudey.
									Getty Images for FLC

schema.headline: Scarlett Johansson Takes Break From Filming Overseas for ‘Paper Tiger’ NYFF Premiere After Skipping Cannes: ‘I’m Hallucinating’

title: Taylor Swift Breaks Two Spotify Records for 2026, Including Most-Streamed Female Artist in a Day
description:
Taylor Swift has broken two Spotify records for 2026, including most-streamed female artist in a day.

	Swift broke the records following the midnig
body:
Taylor Swift has broken two Spotify records for 2026, including most-streamed female artist in a day.

	Swift broke the records following the midnight release of “The Life of a Showgirl: Encore,” which featured four new songs, including lead single “Patient Zero.” That song broke the record for the most-streamed song by a female artist in a day so far this year, while Swift herself had the most streams out of any female artist in a day in 2026.
	

	Swift dropped “The Life of a Showgirl: Encore” after gradually rolling out the promise of new music, beginning with some Easter eggs in a “Law & Order: SVU” skit during the Emmys telecast. In character as a detective, she said, “I think what we’re going to be looking for is hiding in plain sight.” She then broke the fourth wall, looking directly at the camera and saying, “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.” Swifties, of course, solved the puzzle relatively fast, noticing that the third letter of each word spelled out “encore.”


	Then, this past Tuesday, she announced that she would be releasing her new single “Patient Zero” this week, rolling out three limited edition CDs of the single on her website. Just a day later, she revealed that she was actually dropping “The Life of a Showgirl: Encore” on Friday, offering fans four new songs including “Patient Zero,” “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

	On social media, Swift explained why she wanted to add more to her 2025 album. “About a year ago, you guys did a truly unfathomable thing. Something that completely blew my mind… You gave ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ the biggest first week for an album in history,” she wrote. “I took a trip to Sweden to celebrate with Max and Shellback, my two collaborators on this album. Really we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs. I hope you love them, because they were born out of pure gratitude for your exuberance for and celebration of the album we made. ‘The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore’ including four new songs is out on Friday and available to pre-order and save now.”
	

	Up next, Swift is set to debut the video for “Patient Zero” at this Sunday’s MTV VMAs, where she is also being honored with the inaugural Artist-Director Award. She previewed the clip on “CBS Mornings” on Thursday before sharing it on her social media accounts. The video, featuring cinematography by Oscar winner Emmanuel Lubezki, will star Swift alongside Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell.

schema.headline: Taylor Swift Breaks Two Spotify Records for 2026, Including Most-Streamed Female Artist in a Day

title: Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘Unraveled’ Tour Setlist: Every Song Played on Opening Night in Connecticut
description: Olivia Rodrigo officially kicked off the “Unraveled” tour on Friday night with her first show at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford, CT. Scroll down to s
body:
Olivia Rodrigo officially kicked off the “Unraveled” tour on Friday night with her first show at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford, CT. Scroll down to see the setlist as it’s being updated live.

	The 86-date tour is in support of Rodrigo’s third album “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love,” which she released this past June. Following a pair of nights in Hartford, the pop singer will make her way across North America through February 2027, concluding with a 10-night run at both Los Angeles’ Intuit Dome and New York City’s Barclays Center. Then, in March, Rodrigo will jet off to Europe for shows in Amsterdam, Munich and Barcelona before wrapping the tour with a pair of shows at London’s O2 Arena.
	

	Wolf Alice is slated to open on the “Unraveled” tour through the end of October, followed by Devon Again for the remaining North American dates. The Last Dinner Party will join Devon Again as support beginning in January. Across the Pond, Grace Ives will open until April 12, followed by Die Spitz for the rest of the trek.



	Rodrigo already has two tours — “Sour” (2022) and “Guts” (2024-2025) — under her belt. “Guts” was her longest, spanning 102 shows across five continents. It’s currently unknown if Rodrigo plans to add dates in Asia, Australia or South America to the “Unraveled” tour.

	This past August, the singer warmed up for the trek with her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields music festival. Rodrigo personally curated the star-studded, women-only lineup consisting of artists including Chappell Roan, Doechii and Garbage, as well as a closing performance from Rodrigo featuring guest appearances from Alanis Morissette, Sarah McLachlan and Stevie Nicks. All net proceeds were donated to charities that support and advocate for women and girls, and as the evening came to a close, Melinda Gates matched the $10 million already raised and brought the total to $20 million.
	

	See the full setlist for the opening night of Unraveled Tour below, which is divided into seasons (UPDATING LIVE):

	Spring“Drop Dead”“U + Me = <3”“So American”“Good 4 U”“Deja Vu”Summer“My Way”“Serena Joy”“Bad Idea Right”“Ballad of a Homeschooled GIrl”“Vampire”“Purple”Autumn“Stupid Song”“Maggots for Brains”“Traitor”“Begged”“Cigarette Smoke”Winter“Honeybee”“Favorite Crime”“Drivers License”“Less”“The Cure”Encore / Spring“Deja Vu”“All American Bitch”“Expectations”

title: Isaac Mizrahi on the ‘Unzipped’ Restoration, the John Galliano Met Gala Fiasco and Why the ‘Devil Wears Prada’ Cerulean Blue Speech ‘Makes Me Want to Kill Somebody’
description: No doubt Isaac Mizrahi is excited about the release of the newly restored “Unzipped,” the 1995 documentary chronicling a moment in time when he was
body:
No doubt Isaac Mizrahi is excited about the release of the newly restored “Unzipped,” the 1995 documentary chronicling a moment in time when he was one of the fashion world’s hottest designers.

	However, Mizrahi admits he’s not that eager to watch it. “I have to say I hate looking back,” he tells me. “I hate this whole process, a little bit of looking back.”

	What’s so wrong with taking a trip down memory lane?


	“I looked so cute, and I look so shitty now,” the 64-year-old Mizrahi says. “I was so agile, and I’m not as agile anymore. My knees hurt. My back hurts. Even my hair. I had such cute dark hair. Oh, well. But it’s not just vanity. It’s more just about the experience of your life. Thirty years! Man, that is crazy.”
	

	Directed by Mizarahi’s then-boyfriend Douglas Keeves, “Unzipped” chronicles the designer’s planning and execution of the show for his fall 1994 collection.

	The film, which Miramax bought after it was a Sundance hit in 1995, includes appearances by Cindy Crawford, Linda Evangelista, Naomi Campbell, Kate Moss, the late André Leon Talley and Eartha Kitt along with a bevy of other fashion insiders and glitterati.

	The film runs at only 73 minutes. “We didn’t intend to make it that short,” Mizrahi remembers. “We wanted it to be longer. There were about 10 minutes of Faye Dunaway that got out because we couldn’t get the rights to run footage from ‘Mommy Dearest.’”

	What?!

	“She came to a fitting. She was doing a TV pilot, and she needed a lot of suits,” Mizrahi remembers. “We had her for a day and a half, a fitting that was endless. Being the big gay that I am, I was enthralled by every word out of her mouth. One really hilarious thing that I do remember about Faye Dunaway was that she would look in the mirror, and when she liked something, she’d go, ‘Oh, that’s very Faye. Very Faye.’ Talking about herself in the third person was so fantastic. And I do that now. If I like what I look like, I go, ‘Oh, it’s very Faye.’ It’s like I think of myself as Faye Dunaway.”
	

	I ask Mizrahi what he would tell himself if he could go back three decades. Without missing a beat, he says, “’You’re not that fat!’ Swear to God, that’s what I would tell myself. I used to wear these crazy Fred Mertz kind of high-waisted pleated pants that I made myself because I was so fucking crazy that my waist was big. I was so stupid, and I look stupid, I don’t look chic. I look stupid, and I was perfectly fine. I was not fat. But I was a really fat kid, so I lost 75 pounds in high school. I’m never going to get over that. You never do.”

	Mizrahi makes no secret about being on a GLP-1. “I love it,” he coos. “I’m in my 60s, darling and I recently just got so big. I’m usually very good at keeping it under control, but it’s incredible and the rest of your health benefits, it’s incredible.”

	At the height of releasing his eponymous collection, he dressed the A-list, including Sarah Jessica Parker, Nicole Kidman and Natalie Portman. After closing shop in 1998, he released various collections under different monikers or designed for other brands altogether. He also launched a show business career with a cabaret act. Most recently, he appeared in “Marty Supreme” as Gwyneth Paltrow’s press agent.

	Mizrahi is now the creative director at Target and continues to sell a collection on QVC.

	When talking about fashion today, Mizrahi lets out a big sigh. “I don’t know if those giant spectacles they have in Paris and Milan are necessarily supposed to be influential in the way people dress six months later,” he says. “That is why that speech in ‘The Devil Wears Prada’ about cerulean blue makes me want to kill somebody because that is so not the way things work. They want you to believe that’s the way it works. I want to shout that from the rooftops, ‘It never has worked that way — never!’” What those spectacles do is they bolster the image of brand names so that they can sell a ton of perfume and handbags and shoes.”

	When we talked, it was just a few days after The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced it was no longer moving forward with its planned retrospective for John Galliano that would’ve run from May 9, 2027, to Jan. 9, 2028 and served as the theme of next year’s Met Gala. Galliano, who would have been only the third living fashion designer to be feted by the Met following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo in 2017, released a statement on Instagram announcing his decision to pull the retrospective amid backlash over his past racist outbursts.
	

	Galliano makes a brief appearance in “Unzipped” at dinner with Mizrahi, Talley and others in Paris. Mizrahi calls Galliano a “genius,” but also says, “When they announced [the Galliano Met Gala], I thought to myself, ‘Wow, who’s going to that?’ I’m not even talking about Jews or donors of the museum. I’m thinking about a celebrity showing up. I don’t know who would show up on that red carpet. No one is going to say, ‘I love John.’ Who’s going to say that?”

	Next up could for Mizrahi could be a producer’s hat. He’s developing a television series about the life of legendary and very controversial paparazzi photographer Ron Galella with producer Christine Vachon. “We’re doing it with the Ron Galella estate,” he says. “It’s very exciting. We’re in the first, first, first stages, so we haven’t even pitched it or anything yet. But it’s really such a great idea, only because of what it means culturally to our country.”

	“Unzipped” is now showing at the Film Forum in New York City. It will open in Los Angeles at Laemmle Royal and Laemmle Glendale on Oct. 9, followed by a nationwide rollout.

schema.headline: Isaac Mizrahi on the ‘Unzipped’ Restoration, the John Galliano Met Gala Fiasco and Why the ‘Devil Wears Prada’ Cerulean Blue Speech ‘Makes Me Want to Kill Somebody’

title: Paramount Says Timing for Warner Bros. Deal Close ‘If Any’ Is ‘Not Yet Certain’ but Pencils In Oct. 5 Date to Issue PSKY Shareholders Warrants Tied to WBD Merger
description: Paramount Skydance‘s $111 billion agreement to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery is not quite a done deal, but the company is preparing for the deal
body:
Paramount Skydance‘s $111 billion agreement to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery is not quite a done deal, but the company is preparing for the deal to close within the next few weeks.

	In an SEC filing Friday, Paramount said its board on Sept. 25 “determined to voluntarily withdraw the listing of its Class B common stock” from the Nasdaq Global Select Market, under the ticker “PSKY,” and transfer the listing to the New York Stock Exchange. The company expects that the listing and trading of the Class B Common Stock on Nasdaq will end at market close on or about Oct. 5, and that trading will begin on the NYSE at market open on or about Oct. 6.
	

	The board set a record date of the close of business on Oct. 5 for Paramount’s previously announced distribution of warrants giving those holders the option to purchase shares of Class B Common Stock on the NYSE. Those shares would begin trading on Oct. 13.


	However, Paramount noted, “the distribution of the Warrants is contingent on the closing of the previously announced acquisition by the Company of Warner Bros. Discovery” — and that currently, the WBD merger is “subject to further closing conditions, and the ultimate timing for the closing of the WBD Merger, if any, is not yet certain.” 

	As a result, Paramount may choose to “cancel the Record Date and/or the Issue Date or postpone the Record Date and/or the Issue Date to a later date.”

	Also Friday, Warner Bros. Discovery announced that, in connection with the pending Paramount merger, WBD intends to voluntarily delist from Nasdaq its “Euro Notes” debt securities (4.302% senior notes due 2030 and 4.693% senior notes due 2033). To delist the Euro Notes, WBD expects to file a notification “on or around” Oct. 6 with the SEC.
	

	The last hurdle for Paramount’s WBD merger was cleared this week after it reached a settlement with 12 Democratic state attorneys general. If approved by the court, it would drop the antitrust lawsuit the states had filed to block the deal. The judge in the case is still reviewing the proposed settlement, which does not require major concessions from Paramount, and has requested the parties file a response by Monday, Sept. 28, to the request by Sen. Cory Booker (D-N.J.) to launch an independent review of the proposed consent decree.

	Starting Oct. 1, Paramount will being accruing a $7-million-per-day “ticking fee” payable to Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders until the merger closes.

	The warrants to be issued by Paramount to PSKY shareholders are intended to provide eligible holders of its existing Class B Common Stock the opportunity to purchase shares of Class B Common Stock in a new entity “on similar terms” to those offered to the parties in the equity syndicate backing the Warner Bros. Discovery deal, including David Ellison; his father, Larry Ellison; and Gerry Cardinale, head of RedBird Capital Partners.

	The company expects to issue approximately 470 million warrants on Oct. 5. Shares of Class B Common Stock held by the Paramount Global 401(k) Plan and the Paramount Global Master Trust will, in lieu of receiving warrants in the warrant distribution, receive shares of Class B Common Stock.

	According to Paramount, if issued, each warrant initially will entitle the holder to purchase one share of Class B Common Stock at an initial exercise price per share equal to the average of the daily volume-weighted average price of the Class B Common Stock for 20 trading days ending on (and including) the third business day prior to the closing of the WBD merger. The purchase price for the warrants is subject to a maximum of $16.02 per share and a minimum of $12.00 per share.

schema.headline: Paramount Says Timing for Warner Bros. Deal Close ‘If Any’ Is ‘Not Yet Certain’ but Pencils In Oct. 5 Date to Issue PSKY Shareholders Warrants Tied to WBD Merger

title: Inside Ryan Murphy’s Universe: How Director Max Winkler Found Creative Meaning in ‘Lizzie Borden,’ ‘Love Story’ and More
description:
In 2019, Max Winkler was an indie film director about to level up. 

	Having cut his teeth directing sitcoms in the ’10s — including “New Girl,” “Br
body:
In 2019, Max Winkler was an indie film director about to level up. 

	Having cut his teeth directing sitcoms in the ’10s — including “New Girl,” “Brooklyn Nine-Nine” and “Fresh Off the Boat” — 2017’s dark comedy “Flower” was warmly received by audiences. His next film was the gritty boxing drama “Jungleland,” which starred Charlie Hunnam and Jack O’Connell. Debuting at the Toronto International Film Festival, it got solid reviews, and seemed like it could be a commercial hit — maybe even get some awards consideration.
	

	The universe had other plans.


	“I made this movie that I thought was my best movie,” Winkler says. “It came out in the middle of COVID in theaters. It was part of a junk deal from the financier to sell to Paramount. It was so crushing, and I had no money and I had just bought a house and was completely broke. My wife was pregnant at the time. At a certain point — I’m still an artist, but I stopped pretending I was someone else. I stopped pretending like I had to try and be Paul Thomas Anderson, which I’m never gonna be, because there’s only one Paul Thomas Anderson. I became a craftsman in a way, and I was just like, ‘All right, fuck it. I need to make money.’”

	Winkler first entered the Ryan Murphy vast universe of television shows through directing episodes of both “American Horror Stories” and “American Horror Story” in 2021. What he admired about Murphy’s vision was how his fascinations aligned with populist ideas.

	“The interesting thing about Ryan, same thing with Spielberg, is what they’re interested in happens to be the thing that the rest of the world is interested in,” Winkler says. “It’s insane. If I was left to my own devices, my interest is, ‘How do I make it feel like “The Last Detail,” which appeals to you and me and seven other people?’ With kids and the actual fire of ‘No, I have to work,’ I was able to say, ‘How can I take these ideas that are a little bigger than I’m comfortable doing? How can I still make it the way I made my movies, with a specificity and, God willing, a craftsmanship and a level of care?’”
	

	Ultimately, the pair kicked off a robust collaboration that grew and grew, with Winkler directing episodes of and executive producing nearly every Murphy project, from the “Monster” franchise to “Love Story,” “The Shards” to “Feud: Capote vs. The Swans”



	

					“Love Story”
									Michael Parmelee
	



	“I think we both genuinely like to impress one another,” Winkler says. “He writes the script and the scripts are really, really good. Or he does the dramaturgy for it, and says, ‘Are you interested in this?’ If it’s something I feel like I connect to, I love working with him. I find his brain fascinating, and the fact that I happen to find him to be truly singular and brilliant is the first part of it. So when he turns over a script and says, ‘Are you interested?’ I’ll go and I’ll make it, and we’ll talk about it. And we talk about what our influences are and what we want it to feel like. And then I will try really, really, really hard to surprise him and impress him and shock him by the time he sees a cut. We go back and forth and back and forth, and it’s like a dare. My collaboration with him is something that is really important to me.”

	Even though Winkler is in Murphy’s inner circle, the creator is constantly full of surprises, as Murphy takes unexpected turns. For example, Winkler first caught wind of “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story” while in the middle of keeping things running on two wildly different series.

	“I read pages without knowing anything about it,” Winkler says. “I was shooting ‘Love Story’ and I was editing ‘Ed Gein’ at the same time. I thought that maybe ‘Monster’ was going to take a break. And Ryan called me. I knew Ryan and [‘Monster’ showrunner] Ian [Brennan] were thinking about a different version of the show with some different people involved. He called me and said, ‘What do you know about Lizzie Borden?’ I was immediately floored by the rhythms of the writing, the sense of humor and the energy and the femininity of it. I felt so much empathy for Lizzie, and who she is when we meet her. Ian and Ryan are genuinely funny human beings, and I could feel their black humor in this — and it excited me tremendously.”



	

					“Monster: The Ed Gein Story”
									COURTESY OF NETFLIX
	



	That penchant for dark humor reverberates through Winkler onto the set. Hunnam, who became friends with Winkler after “Jungleland,” and has worked with him such on projects as “Ed Gein” and “Lizzie Borden,” says that Winkler’s wit helped formalize the tricky tone on “Lizzie Borden.”
	

	“One of the great joys of my career is getting to make Max laugh,” Hunnam says. “He laughs a lot during takes behind the monitor, and you try with something that you think is going to be funny and play it out. Whether you hear that laugh or you don’t is a barometer of how successful you’ve been. If we were making him laugh, we felt like, ‘All right, this is probably on the right track.’”

	Despite his laughter, Ella Beatty, who plays Lizzie, says that Winkler also has an openness that allowed her to experiment in portraying the complex character.

	“He has such a spirit of play and emotional availability,” she says. “So there really was an environment of trusting what happened and getting really specific on your homework in the beginning, so that you can come in and not show any of it and you can just play.”



	

					“Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story”
									Courtesy of Netflix
	



	Working so closely on so many of Murphy’s shows not only gave Winkler a creative charge — “OK, I can express myself in a different way and still do what I do well” — but the newfound spotlight of high-profile projects also gave him an exciting new relationship with art.

	“I want to make really good things for people that actually get to go and see them, because I’ve never had that experience,” he says. “I didn’t know you got to talk about the things you made while they were out. These last few years, I’ve made things — between ‘Ed Gein’ and ‘Love Story’ and, I hope, ‘Lizzie’ — where I’m actually getting to interact with people in its intended window. It’s delightful. A really nice part of it is to just feel like you exist. You’re embarrassed to admit it sometimes, but you do want people to see this shit. You work so hard on it, and in your greatest moments, you feel like Orson Welles. In your worst moments, you feel like the biggest fucking loser hack of all time. Being present in the process and not making anything for a result is super important. But having kids allowed me to say yes to things that I was afraid to say yes to because I was an idiot, and still find a way to express myself and build a career that I have now, which is way different from when I was in film school and had a very small view of what a career could look like.”

	This interview has been edited and condensed.

schema.headline: Inside Ryan Murphy’s Universe: How Director Max Winkler Found Creative Meaning in ‘Lizzie Borden,’ ‘Love Story’ and More

title: ‘Love Hypothesis’ Director Claire Scanlon Breaks Down the Biggest ‘Star Wars’ Easter Eggs, From Gracie Abrams’ Song to Color-Coded Wardrobes
description: “Star Wars” has featured iconic locations throughout the franchise, taking audiences to Tatooine, Naboo and now, a campus biology lab at Stanford Un
body:
“Star Wars” has featured iconic locations throughout the franchise, taking audiences to Tatooine, Naboo and now, a campus biology lab at Stanford University.

	The romantic comedy “Love Hypothesis” premiered on Amazon Prime on Sept. 23, featuring Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman as romantic interests who get caught in a fake-dating-turned-real-love trope. On the surface, there is no obvious connection to George Lucas’ franchise, but the story’s origin is actually deeply rooted in a galaxy far, far away.
	

	Ali Hazelwood’s 2021 source novel of the same name was originally written as a fan fiction about the “Star Wars” sequel trilogy’s Kylo Ren and Rey, titled “Head Over Feet.” She ultimately transformed her 2018 narrative into a New York Times bestselling novel years later, removing the most obvious “Star Wars” references. But those familiar with the story’s source material will be able to spot plenty of Jedi-adjacent references throughout the romantic comedy.


	Claire Scanlon, the film’s director, took a break from filming her next project, the Netflix comedy series “I Suck at Girls,” to break down the “Star Wars” references featured in “Love Hypothesis.” She reveals she wasn’t initially aware the plot was based on a fanfiction between Kylo and Rey, let alone the novel’s popularity on BookTok, a TikTok community that shares reading recommendations with each other.

	“Elizabeth [Cantillon, the film’s producer] said, ‘This is based on a book about “Star Wars” fan fiction and it’s from BookTok,’” Scanlon says while laughing. “And I was like, ‘I understand none of the words you just said to me.’”
	

	Perhaps the most overt nod to the galactic universe is the casting of Bateman, who plays the hard-shelled Kylo Ren-inspired Adam Carlsen. In real life, the actor is married to Daisy Ridley, who originated the role of Rey, though Scanlon confirms this connection didn’t influence his casting.

	Fans may have also picked up on the film’s opening song, “Mess It Up” by Gracie Abrams, whose father, J.J. Abrams, directed two films in the most recent “Star Wars” trilogy. But it wasn’t Scanlon who came up with this subtle nod, which she reveals was flagged by observant fans on social media.

	“Someone on TikTok or Instagram said, ‘They better use a Gracie Abrams song.’ And I was like, ‘Why would they want to use a Gracie Abrams song?’” she says, laughing about her initial cluelessness.

	Below, Scanlon breaks down the biggest nod to “Star Wars” in “Love Hypothesis,” and debunks some of the speculated references circulating online.



	

					Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman in “The Love Hypothesis”
									©Amazon/Courtesy Everett Collection
	


	
		Color Schemes	

	Bateman’s character, Adam, is a clear reference to Kylo Ren, as well as nods from his intimidating demeanor to his telling nickname, “Dr. Evil.” Scanlon confirms that Adam also channels the character through his all-black wardrobe, which is mirrored by his minimally decorated office that features an almost entirely black color scheme.

	Reinhart’s character, Olive Smith, is primarily seen wearing her lab coat, but outside of the laboratory, she is dressed in red, blue and green outfits. Although these are all colors associated with different lightsabers, that choice was unintentional, Scanlon says. Some eagle-eyed fans also noted she frequently wears an all-red look, which is the color associated with Rey in “The Rise of Skywalker,” though Scanlon says that was just a coincidence.

	“Lili just likes the color red,” she says while laughing. “This is nuts. I got to tell Lili all these!”

	While this isn’t a reference to Kylo Ren, Scanlon also points out that as Adam spends more time with Olive, his color palette begins to soften from black to navy blue. The texture of his clothes also evolves from cold, hard fabrics to cashmere and softer clothes, representing Olive’s positive impact on him.
	
		Using the Name “Adam”	

	Yes, Scanlon confirms the character Adam Carlsen is, in fact, named after Adam Driver, who originated the role of Kylo Ren. But the director also has a question for Hazelwood about some other characters. 
	

	“I know Ali named Adam after Adam Driver, but did she name Tom Benton after Tom Bateman? The bad guy?” she asks, laughing. “Was she trying to push them apart? Was it just a coincidence? Or was she hating on Tom for being with Daisy and wanted Daisy and Adam Driver to be together?
	
		“Star Wars” Soundtrack	

	Several moments throughout the film feature John Williams’ “Star Wars” themes, further emphasizing the parallels. “Star Wars” composer John Williams’ theme for Kylo Ren plays when Adam enters the coffee shop with Olive, causing the customers to freeze in fear.

	The fallen Jedi’s theme is used again near the end of the film when Adam goes to confront his colleague Tom. The director also points out that this scene was filmed from a low angle as Adam menacingly walks down an empty hallway, visually mirroring several shots of Kylo in the “Star Wars” films.

	Viewers also pointed out that a sample of “Rey’s Theme” was used when Olive tells her friends details of her relationship with Adam after they find the couple in the coffee shop. Scanlon says she doesn’t know if this was intentional, but it could’ve been slipped in from the music team.

	“This is fun,” Scanlon says before breaking down the next reference. “This is like a game!”



	

					Lili Reinhart in “The Love Hypothesis”
									©Amazon/Courtesy Everett Collection
	


	
		Olive’s Hairstyle	

	Olive frequently wears her hair in a high bun, which Scanlon confirms is a nod to Rey’s signature hairstyle of three buns on top of her head.
	
		Adam Carrying Olive	

	One of the moments when the dynamic between Kylo and Rey shifted in the “Star Wars” films came when Kylo carried an injured Rey onto his ship, hinting at his romantic feelings for her. A similar moment occurs in “The Love Hypothesis” when Adam carries Olive after her feet begin to hurt following their sushi date.

	Although the scene mirrors the Kylo and Ren dynamic of alluding to the eventual shift in their relationship, Scanlon isn’t certain that choice was intentional. As far as she knows, it wasn’t a designated reference, but screenwriter Sarah Rothschild may have slyly incorporated the moment.



	

					Tom Bateman and Lili Reinhart in “The Love Hypothesis”
									©Amazon/Courtesy Everett Collection
	


	
		Adam’s Speech About Being Evil	

	During their date at the sushi restaurant, Adam opens up to Olive about how he never intended to be evil. He shared that his mentor was a sadist who had powerful friends in high places, very similar to Kylo Ren’s corruption after being mentored by Supreme Leader Snoke. This scene was directly taken from the book, Scanlon says, so it was likely a reference created by Hazelwood. 
	

	In that same scene, Adam also jokingly calls Olive a rebel, which could be a nod to Rey’s allegiance to the Resistance. Scanlon isn’t certain if that’s an intentional reference, noting this may also have been a choice by Rothschild.

	Watch “The Love Hypothesis” trailer below.

schema.headline: ‘Love Hypothesis’ Director Claire Scanlon Breaks Down the Biggest ‘Star Wars’ Easter Eggs, From Gracie Abrams’ Song to Color-Coded Wardrobes

title: ‘Control Resonant’ Team on ‘Reverse Symmetry’ of Switching From Jesse to Dylan as Sequel Game’s New Protagonist
description:
Following a nearly seven-year development journey, Remedy Entertainment has unleashed the sequel to its 2019 hit video game “Control.”

	Released Th
body:
Following a nearly seven-year development journey, Remedy Entertainment has unleashed the sequel to its 2019 hit video game “Control.”

	Released Thursday for Steam, the Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, “Control Resonant” picks up after Jesse Faden, the protagonist of the original “Control” game, goes missing upon the conclusion of the events at The Oldest House. 


	The main character for the “Control” sequel is Jesse’s younger brother, Dylan Faden (played by Sean Durrie), who battles a preternatural crisis engulfing a reality-warped Manhattan, unleashing his powers and mastering the different forms of his shape-shifting melee weapon, the Aberrant, to face dangerous enemies and monumental bosses. 
	

	“There’s this interesting kind of reverse symmetry when you look at both games,” “Control” franchise creative director and Remedy co-creative director Mikael Kasurinen tells Variety. “In the first game, Jesse arrives at The Oldest House looking for Dylan, trying to understand what happened to her brother. And her arc obviously then becomes a lot about herself, in many different ways. While she’s trying to look for Dylan and understand what’s going on, she becomes the director of this strange bureau called the Bureau of Control and it was, in a way, her fate to become that person. In a way, she found a place to be and she was happy inside The Oldest House.”

	For “Control Resonant,” Kasurinen says “we turn it the other way around.”

	“Jesse is missing, lost, we don’t know what’s going on with her and Dylan wakes up and then he starts his search for her and trying to understand again what is happening in the world,” Kasurinen says. “And he ends up dealing with the imminent threats and he finds Zoe, as Jesse found Pope early on [in ‘Control’]. So there’s a lot of this interesting symmetry between the characters and their journeys. But of course, Dylan’s thing is to try to find connections and a sense of belonging and all of those things that are unique to him and his arc. And as he searches for Jesse, we unlock more and more what she’s doing, what she’s dealing with and so on. And we start to understand her choices as well that she took early on in the story. Going further than that would be spoiling it, but both stories revolve around both siblings, and we just basically switch sides in a way.”
	

	“Control Resonant” star Durrie says when he was brought on for the original game, the team prepared him for the idea of Dylan taking the lead in the sequel.

	“When they told me about the project and were pitching it to me, we got to the very end and they’re like, ‘And he’s not dead. He’s in a coma,’” Durrie says. “And so while they didn’t get into the details of where we are today, I knew that they had things up their sleeve right at the beginning.”

	Durrie says he used some details from the first “Control” to develop Dylan’s character for “Resonant,” but notes that much of his previous performance wasn’t carried over due to the state of mind Dylan is in when the franchise begins — namely, being controlled by The Hiss.

	“I took, in particular, the events of the first game of why he was victimized, letting the Hiss in, his guilt from that, his need for atonement and then now his need to want to rediscover his humanity,” Durrie says. “So I took his backstory of living in this house since he was 10, and then at one point in time, getting thrown into a cell and forgotten about and so that’s where we really started to find the bits that really made it through to the second game. Performance-wise, he’s infected by The Hiss in the original ‘Control,’ so he doesn’t act like that anymore, but his memory of it is, his guilt, quite frankly, of it and what he did, even if it wasn’t under his control and what the end result was and now telling the story of him rediscovering himself.”

	It’s not only the main POV that the “Control” team has changed for “Resonant,” but also some of the game mechanics.

	“In regard to the first game, having this sense of fast-paced, first-person action was already a key thing,” Kasurinen says. “Combining the use of a weapon with preternatural abilities, all of those elements were already there and we knew that. And I think that’s a kind of a ‘Control’ recipe, in many ways. And it sounds like a small thing, but of course it is a bigger thing that we switched the weapon. Instead of a gun, Dylan uses a melee weapon. And we wanted to go a lot further into how you can feel like you jump into this interesting, colorful sandbox and making sure that the environments are as versatile as they can be and find many different ways for Dylan to navigate those environments, including being able to utilize the gravity anomalies through shift and attach himself to different surfaces. And then to create an interesting wide range of different types of enemies for you to fight against, and also avoid. Like in the first game, that we don’t get stuck with one single enemy, but it’s more like a composition of enemies that you have to face. I think that larger philosophy was already there in the first game, and I think we were able to go a lot further into that direction with the second game.”
	

	For those completely new to the world of “Control,” the sequel game is sure to be a challenge, but the creative team has found one way to make it a little easier to enter without all the proper backstory. 

	“Zoe’s character will be helpful if this is the first venture you’ve had into ‘Control,’” Durrie says. “She’s kind of asking the questions that you may be asking. But if you are well-versed in the lore of ‘Control,’ you’ll jump right in. So either way, we’re ready for people to play.”

	“Zoe is, of course, a big new character,” Kasurinen adds. “Crucial for Dylan, crucial for the storytelling and all of those elements. It’s very much the player perspective into the situation. Like, what the hell is The Hiss? And who’s Jesse? Who are you?”

title: Five Hilton All-Inclusive Resorts for Destination Weddings: From Mexico to the Dominican Republic
description:
Sep 25, 2026 4:36pm PT	
	


		Five Hilton All-Inclusive Resorts for Destination Weddings: From Mexico to the Dominican Republic
body:
Sep 25, 2026 4:36pm PT Five Hilton All-Inclusive Resorts for Destination Weddings: From Mexico to the Dominican Republic If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. Celebrities have long understood that sometimes the best wedding venue requires a passport. George and Amal Clooney turned Venice into the backdrop for their multi-day 2014 celebration, Priyanka Chopra and Nick Jonas took over Jodhpur’s Umaid Bhawan Palace for their lavish 2018 nuptials, and Kourtney Kardashian and Travis Barker brought their guests to Portofino for an elaborately styled Italian wedding weekend in 2022. John Legend and Chrissy Teigen, meanwhile, chose a villa on Lake Como for their 2013 ceremony. You don’t, however, need a Kardashian-sized production team to pull off a wedding that doubles as a vacation. Hilton’s roster of all-inclusive resorts across Mexico and the Caribbean offers a more turnkey approach to the destination wedding, pairing beachfront ceremony sites and sprawling reception venues with dedicated event teams, customizable wedding packages and the biggest logistical perk of all: once guests arrive, much of the trip is already taken care of. That means couples can spend less time coordinating separate tabs for welcome drinks, group dinners and poolside margaritas and more time actually celebrating. Dining, drinks, activities and entertainment are included at the resorts, while select wedding packages can cover everything from officiants and florals to cocktail hours, three-course receptions, DJs, photography and even fireworks. Whether the vision is a barefoot ceremony overlooking the Caribbean, a full-scale ballroom bash in Tulum or a wedding weekend tucked away on a quieter stretch of Dominican coastline, these Hilton all-inclusive resorts are particularly well suited to turning the big day into a full-fledged group getaway — and all bookable on Hilton.com. Best for large wedding groups: Hilton Cancun, an All-Inclusive ResortBest for an expansive wedding weekend: Hilton Tulum Riviera Maya All-Inclusive ResortBest for flexible ceremony styles: Hilton Vallarta Riviera All-Inclusive ResortBest for indoor and outdoor settings: Hilton Cancun Mar Caribe All-Inclusive ResortBest for a secluded ceremony: Zemi Miches Punta Cana All-Inclusive Resort, Curio Collection by Hilton BEST FOR LARGE GROUPS Hilton Cancun, an All-Inclusive Resort For couples who want a classic Cancun beach wedding but need enough infrastructure for a sizable guest list, Hilton Cancun is one of the portfolio’s most expansive options. The beachfront property has nearly 70,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor event space, meaning a wedding can move from a ceremony on the sand to cocktails in a sunlit foyer and, finally, a full ballroom reception without guests ever leaving the resort.Hilton’s Signature package includes a bilingual officiant, private cocktail reception and wedding cake, while upgraded packages add private receptions, audio equipment and perks such as early check-in and late checkout. The resort also offers wedding-adjacent touches including room upgrades and anniversary-stay benefits.The setup also makes it easy to occupy guests outside the wedding itself. The all-inclusive offering spans 12 dining experiences aincluding wood-fired pizza and Italian dishes at La Luce, plus Mexican and international options; two infinity pools; beach and poolside service; yoga; nightly entertainment; and kids and teens clubs. Twenty-four-hour room service is also included, making late-night post-reception meals one less thing to organize. best for expansive wedding weekend Hilton Tulum Riviera Maya All-Inclusive Resort Hilton Tulum Riviera Maya is better suited to couples who want the lush, slightly more secluded aesthetic associated with Tulum.Couples can exchange vows directly on the beach before moving into a cocktail reception and dinner by the sea, while larger celebrations have access to the resort’s shared 50,000-square-foot event center. Its Tulkal ballroom alone spans about 31,000 square feet, while the Tulkalito ballroom can accommodate a reception of more than 900 guests.There are four main wedding-package tiers, with inclusions becoming increasingly elaborate. The Devotion package, for example, includes a symbolic ceremony performed by a bilingual officiant, ceremony audio, a one-hour cocktail reception with an open bar and hors d’oeuvres, and a three-hour private reception with a three-course meal. Higher tiers can add an arch and aisle runner, photography, a DJ, live music, dance floor, rehearsal dinner and pyrotechnics.And because a destination wedding is rarely just one night, there’s plenty to keep everyone occupied during the rest of the trip. Among the dining standouts are Auma, a steakhouse focused on grilled cuts and seasonal sides; Noriku, for sushi and sashimi; Mexican-fusion grill Chiringuito Seasalt; and La Churreria, where the menu is essentially the dream post-wedding fare of unlimited ice cream and churros. The resort also has nine pools, including quieter areas and a splash zone for kids, plus beach volleyball, yoga, cultural workshops and nightly entertainment. Guests booking the upgraded Enclave category get access to two additional private pools and exclusive dining at Cocomar. MOST FLEXIBLE CEREMONY STYLES Hilton Vallarta Riviera All-Inclusive Resort
On Mexico’s Pacific coast, Hilton Vallarta Riviera swaps Cancun’s Caribbean blues for the Bay of Banderas, golden sunsets and the surrounding Sierra Madre Mountains — a particularly photogenic combination for couples who want their ceremony scenery to do much of the decorating for them.The resort has an 11,840-square-foot convention center as well as a 16,469-square-foot Beach Club, with 10 flexible convention-center venues capable of hosting groups of up to 900. The latter also gives couples an oceanfront setting for outdoor receptions rather than limiting the celebration to a conventional ballroom.Hilton Vallarta Riviera also stands out for the range of ceremonies its team explicitly accommodates. The resort welcomes LGBTQ+ weddings with Equality Institute-certified planners and says its event team is versed in cultural and faith traditions from around the world. Depending on the couple’s plans and applicable local requirements, the resort can help coordinate symbolic, non-denominational and select legal ceremoniesIts Signature, Devotion, Cherish and Cherish Captured packages scale from relatively streamlined ceremonies and cocktail hours to four-hour private receptions with three-course meals, DJs, live music, dance floors, photography and outdoor fountain fireworks. The higher-end packages can also include a semi-private rehearsal dinner for up to 30 people, wedding-day getting-ready room and room upgrades for members of the wedding party.Dining can also become part of the wedding weekend, with restaurants highlighting regional Mexican cuisine, Italian favorites, seafood and poolside beverages. There are 12 restaurants and bars, including six specialty restaurants: Maxal moves through regional Mexican cooking, from Mexico City street food to Oaxacan mole and Michoacán-style carnitas, while La Luce serves Italian and Italian-American dishes from an artisanal stone oven. Hilton also highlights fresh seafood at Cocomar, and drinks extend beyond the usual frozen resort cocktail with premium wines, spirits and made-to-order tropical drinks delivered poolside. INDOOR AND OUTDOOR SETTINGS Hilton Cancun Mar Caribe All-Inclusive Resort
Hilton Cancun Mar Caribe is a strong option for couples who want the convenience of Cancun but envision something more varied than a ceremony and reception entirely on the sand.Beachfront vows are certainly an option, but the resort also has indoor venues with ocean views and elevated outdoor spaces. Its Chala Sky Bar, for example, can be transformed into an open-air reception overlooking the Caribbean — an appealing change of scenery for couples who want the water in the background without spending the entire evening barefoot in the sand.Hilton offers four all-inclusive wedding packages at the resort, letting couples bundle the ceremony and many of the surrounding details rather than source them individually. The broader Hilton package structure can incorporate everything from wedding cakes and sparkling-wine toasts to private meals, music, photography and customizable extras.For guests, accommodations make the plane ticket worth it. The real differentiator here is the resort’s sheer amount of water: 13 pools, ranging from lively family areas to quieter places to retreat after the reception, plus a kids’ splash pool with water slides. When guests finally dry off, there are 12 restaurants and bars and five specialty dining experiences. Maxal serves Mexican dishes using locally sourced ingredients, while Seasalt handles poolside pizza and snacks; there are also Italian and Asian restaurants, a steakhouse and Azulinda Café, a 24-hour stop for coffee, sandwiches and sweets. Activities include mini-golf, cooking classes, casino nights, beach volleyball, yoga and aqua aerobics, while live mariachi and pop-up performances continue into the evenings.Couples can also book Honeymoon Suites with private balconies and spa-style soaking tubs overlooking the water. BEST FOR A SECLUDED CEREMONY Zemi Miches Punta Cana All-Inclusive Resort, Curio Collection by Hilton For couples looking beyond the Dominican Republic’s busier resort areas, Zemi Miches offers a more secluded setting along Playa Esmeralda, surrounded by ocean, mountains and tropical landscape — or simply want somewhere that feels farther removed from its busiest resort strips — Zemi Miches offers a more secluded Dominican Republic setting on Playa Esmeralda, with the ocean in front and the mountains and tropical landscape surrounding the resort.Weddings can begin directly on the beach before moving into cocktails and a private reception, and every celebration is assigned a dedicated Event Manager who works with the couple on the details from the planning stage through the wedding itself.The packages are unusually comprehensive. Depending on the tier selected, couples can arrange an arch and aisle runner, ceremony photography, a private cocktail hour with an open bar and passed hors d’oeuvres, a multi-course private reception, DJ and live musician, dance floor and several hours of photography. Some packages also include a rehearsal dinner for up to 30 guests, a getting-ready room, hair and makeup, room upgrades and breakfast in the couple’s room the morning after the wedding.Dining is a notable part of the experience, with 17 restaurants, bars and lounges inspired by Caribbean, Taíno, Thai and Amalfi Coast flavors. Guests can move between beachfront grills and destination restaurants before ending up at one of the resort’s swim-up bars, while 24-hour room service covers anyone who misses dinner because the reception went long. Ready to start planning? Explore each resort’s wedding venues and current packages, then connect directly with the property’s wedding team for availability, pricing and celebration details. Wedding guests can book their stays directly through Hilton.com or the Hilton Honors app. More from Variety

title: Wisconsin Frat Leaders Arrested After Cops Find Teen Pledges Covered in Food in Basement
description:
Univ. of Wisconsin Frat Leaders
                          Arrested in Alleged Hazing Incident
body:
Univ. of Wisconsin Frat Leaders
                          Arrested in Alleged Hazing Incident
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Two frat leaders in Wisconsin have been arrested after cops found dozens of half-naked pledges in a basement, covered in food.
      
    
            20-year-olds Brayden J. Klein and Samuel N. Vane -- leaders of a reportedly unrecognized University of Wisconsin frat -- were booked Wednesday for misdemeanor hazing and misdemeanor disorderly conduct in the alleged hazing incident.
      
    
            According to the New York Post, cops found 30 teens in the basement of the Alpha Epsilon Pi frat house ... noting in the report that they were covered in food and condiments, and some had "visible injuries consistent with being physically assaulted."
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Police say the thermostat had been set to 81 degrees, making the room uncomfortably hot and muggy.
      
    
            Cops say they escorted everyone out of the building, noting a "vast majority" of pledges were only 18 years old.
      
    
            According to police, the frat is "unrecognized and unaccredited" with the university ... and the school had actually stopped recognizing them over a decade ago.
      
    
            The University of Wisconsin said in a statement Thursday ... "UW–Madison is fully committed to preventing and addressing hazing and takes all incidents involving our community seriously."
      
    
            The statement continued ... "Any student determined to be in violation of law, regulation, or university policy may be subject to sanctions according to Wis. Admin. Code Chapter UWS 17."
      
    
            The school says the sanctions could range from a written reprimand to termination or educational sanctions.

title: R&B Singer Keke Wyatt Allegedly Threatened to Shoot Woman Before Assault Arrest
description:
R&B Star Keke Wyatt Arrest
                          Allegedly Threatened to Shoot Woman ...
body:
R&B Star Keke Wyatt Arrest
                          Allegedly Threatened to Shoot Woman ...
                          'I Can Blow Her Brains Out'
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            R&B sensation Keke Wyatt allegedly threatened to put a bullet in another woman's head ... allegedly extending a gun out of her car window while shouting out warnings ... this according to her arrest warrant.
      
    
            We've obtained the affidavit from the warrant that lays out law enforcement's version of events leading up to Keke's arrest earlier this week ... with an officer claiming they were dispatched to an area in Georgia on September 20 regarding an alleged domestic disturbance.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to the docs, the incident apparently went down between two people during a custody exchange ... with cops saying Keke was also there, but wasn't one of the two people involved in the exchange.
      
    
            Cops say a witness told them they saw a fight break out between the two people ... before Keke allegedly pulled out a black 9mm Beretta and pointed it through the window of the car.
      

            The witness told cops they saw Keke extend the gun out of the car window and shout, "Let that bitch come over here, so I can blow her brains out."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Cops say Keke admitted to holding the gun ... but denied pointing it out the window or making any threats.
      
    
            As we reported ... she was arrested and booked on charges of terroristic threats, simple assault, and cruelty to children. The report says three children were nearby when the alleged incident occurred, hence the cruelty to children charge.
      
    
            Keke was arrested and released 2 days later after posting a $1,050 bond.

title: Joshua Jackson Allegedly Had Concerns About Kid Being Around Jodie Turner-Smith's Bro
description:

                          Concerned About Kid Being Around Jodie Turner-Smith's Br
body:
Joshua Jackson
                          Concerned About Kid Being Around Jodie Turner-Smith's Bro?!?
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Joshua Jackson raised concerns about his daughter being around Jodie Turner-Smith's brother long before three women sued the actress and her bro over his alleged drug-fueled sex parties ... according to the attorney representing the women suing the siblings.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... Jodie and her brother, Richard Mark Anthony Smith, were sued by three Jane Does who claim Richard pressured them into drug use and nonconsensual sexual activity.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The lawsuit also alleges Jodie knowingly provided her brother with housing, money, and other support despite his alleged behavior. Through her reps, Jodie has denied the allegations, calling them false, and claimed the lawsuit was actually filed by a man who was harassing the actress.
      
    
            Now, plaintiffs' attorney Nissan Thomas is firing back in a statement to TMZ ... he claims sources close to the family told his office Joshua had concerns about Richard being around his daughter, Juno, who he shares with Jodie.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to Thomas, those sources allege Joshua's attorneys raised similar issues during the former couple's divorce and custody proceedings. Thomas also claims he was told some of the concerns included Jodie allegedly allowing Richard to pick Juno up from school despite Richard allegedly not having a driver's license.
